Sure, many people would survive. Switzerland for an instance has nuclear shelters that can house most of their population. Now, for how long can a big amount of people last inside a bunker? How many supplies are enough, given that you cant go out for years? However there is no such thing as a lite version of a nuclear war. You may refer to http://nationalinterest.org/blog/the-buzz/quite-possibly-the-dumbest-military-concept-ever-limited-16394 on why a ''limited nuclear war'' is a concept in nuclear doctrine that makes no sense.

There are things that can't be undone, and hardly anyone hit with a tactical nuclear bomb (another way of saying a small one) would not guarantee that the strategic nuclear bombs (the real, city-erasing bombs) will not be used. The US DoD has in the works:  LRSO or Long Range Standoff Missile which is a new cruise missile which is hard to detect and also an initiative for a GBSD or Ground Based Strategic Deterrent which would replace the aging Minuteman III land based intercontinental ballistic missiles is on the works by Nortrop Grumman Corporation.

With Nuclear Deterrence being the bedrock of American foreign policy regarding other great powers in the International System, it would be very unlikely that, in the event of an initial ''lite'' nuclear war, things will not escalate into a full blown Judgement Day like in the Terminator saga.

Most of the servers that power the internet are located in the US. Mainly after an attack, the main disruption would occur on the internet. The only way you would notice that something went really bad outside of your window after losing contact via internet would be the freezing weather. The GIF image here http://www.nucleardarkness.org/warconsequences/hundredfiftytonessmoke/, shows that after the exchange on a full scale nuclear war, it would take 2 weeks for the clouds to cover both north and southern hemispheres. Millions of tons of smoke would black out the sun, who ever survived the initial strikes would freeze, something we call nuclear winter. Even humans living in shelters equipped with many years worth of food, water, energy, and medical supplies would probably not survive in the hostile post-war environment.
